title: Looking for Something That May Not Exist

sections.title: The rule
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* from B1 Unit 5 and the present subjunctive from A2 Unit 27. Now put them together. English uses the same verb in both cases: "I'm looking for a flat that has a balcony" can mean any flat at all, or one you already know about. Spanish makes you choose. If you cannot point at the thing, because you are only looking for it, hoping for it or not sure it exists, the verb after *que* goes into the subjunctive. If the thing is real and you know it, the verb stays in the indicative.

sections.title: Real, or not found yet?
rows: Busco un apartamento que tenga balcón.
I'm looking for a flat with a balcony (any flat; I don't know if there is one).
Tengo un apartamento que tiene balcón.
I have a flat that has a balcony (a real flat).
Necesito una persona que hable inglés.
I need someone who speaks English (whoever it turns out to be).
Conozco a una persona que habla inglés.
I know someone who speaks English (a real person).

sections.title: Nothing there to point at
sections.content: A negative sentence says that the thing does not exist, so there is nothing real for *que* to describe. That also takes the subjunctive: *No hay nadie que sepa la respuesta* means "There is nobody who knows the answer". You know *nadie*, *nada* and *ningún* from A2 Unit 31; the next lesson gives them more room.

items.spanish: Busco a alguien que me ayude.
items.english: I'm looking for someone to help me.

items.spanish: Encontré a alguien que me ayuda.
items.english: I found someone who helps me.

items.spanish: No hay nadie que sepa la respuesta.
items.english: There is nobody who knows the answer.

items.spanish: No tengo ningún libro que explique eso.
items.english: I don't have any book that explains that.

sections.content: Ask yourself one question: can I point at it? If you can name it, see it or hold it, use the indicative. If it is only wanted, needed or imagined, or if you say it does not exist, use the subjunctive. English gives you no clue, so the decision is yours. You know the personal *a* from A1 Unit 24; keep it before a person: *Busco a alguien que…*, *No conozco a nadie que…*.
